newsitem.title: GERMANY: German premium coffee roaster sees higher 96 sales.
newsitem.headline: German premium coffee roaster sees higher 96 sales.

text.p: The chairman of German premium coffee roaster J.J. Darboven, Albert Darboven, said he expected higher volume sales in the group's roasted coffee products this year.

"We hope for a 15 percent volume increase in 1996 but sales revenue won't increase by the same amount," he told Reuters during a promotional event to boost Christmas sales of so-called fairly-priced coffee.
The company has a seven percent market share in Germany and last year sold 24,000 tonnes of roasted coffee worth 469 million marks.
It has a large presence in coffee vending outside grocery chains such as canteens, airlines and hotels.
Darboven products cost an average 6.99-8.99 marks per 0.5 kg compared with a retail market average of just under seven marks, but appeal to quality-conscious consumers.
The managing director of German coffee association DKV, Frieder Rotzoll, said the general market did not share this optimism.
"Young consumers are not entering the coffee market at the same stage and with the same demand intensity as older generations used to do," he told Reuters.
Coffee sales volumes should be steady this year at 1995's 564,000 tonnes green coffee value, he reiterated after earlier DKV projections for stable sales.
But per-capita consumption would be lower because households in 1995 used up coffees hoarded during the 1994 high price phase, research now showed.
Darboven as a licensee of the TransFair project last year sold some 600 tonnes of coffee under a fair-trade label, where guaranteed returns are passed on to support smallholders and co-operatives.

Albert Darboven said the idea was catching on and the market share of "fairly" traded coffee might rise to four or five percent in Germany within the next four or five years. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
